findings.title: The page does not say what the 30-day trial costs or commits the owner to, and nothing backs up the promise

location.description: the area under the "Start a 30-day trial" button and the empty space below the feature lines

findings.viewer_experience: The owner cannot tell whether the 30-day trial is a free month or a first paid month. The nav links "Pricing" and "Shops using it" go to nothing on this page, and the page ends before it makes its case.

current.value: no trial terms, no comparison, no price, no named shop under the button or below the feature lines

findings.target: One line of trial terms directly under the button, and proof in the empty space below the feature lines: a comparison with how the owner now decides what to reorder, and the price or a real shop.
findings.fix_direction: Add one line of trial terms under the button. Use the empty space for a comparison with how the owner now decides what to reorder, and add the price or a real shop. The maker must supply every fact: whether the trial is free, whether a card is needed, what happens after day 30, the price, and which shops use it.

closed_when.check: In the new image at the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, a fresh critic sees a line of trial terms directly under the "Start a 30-day trial" button and proof content (comparison, price or a named shop) in the space below the feature lines.

findings.title: The second feature line on the tablet is 76 characters per line, one over the target

location.description: the second feature line, "Orders from your distributor..."

findings.viewer_experience: The line runs one character longer than the comfortable reading measure.
findings.fix_direction: Bring the width cap down a little more, from 560 px to about 550 px.

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of section.facts > p:nth-of-type(2) in the tablet viewport is 75 or fewer

findings.title: On the phone the "Sold this week" column ends about 8 px from the right edge of the card

location.description: the "Sold this week" column of the table on the phone

findings.viewer_experience: The last column sits tight against the right edge of the card and does not match the left edge.

current.value: cell box [254, 607, 116, 40] runs past the card's inner edge at 366 px; about 8 px from the card edge

findings.target: About 12 px of right padding on the last cell, matching the left edge of the card
findings.fix_direction: Give the last cell about 12 px of right padding.

closed_when.check: the right edge of thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(3) text in the phone viewport is at or inside the card's inner edge at 366 px, and a fresh critic sees about 12 px of space between "Sold this week" and the card edge

findings.title: The reorder table has three columns and nothing says whether the product suggests an order quantity
findings.viewer_experience: The table lists stock and sales but not how many copies to order, so the owner cannot tell what to do with a row.

current.value: 3 columns: Title, On shelf, Sold this week

findings.target: The table matches what the product does about order quantity.
findings.fix_direction: The maker must say whether the product suggests how many copies to order. If it does, add that column. If it does not, leave the table as it is.

closed_when.check: In the new image at the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, the maker has answered the question: either the table has an order quantity column, or the maker has confirmed the product does not suggest one and the table is unchanged.
